source: Zhang, Liang, Zhou, Ahmad, Waseem (2023), IJSEKE 33(11-12):1653-1672, arXiv 2309.05687; Zenodo 8123303, 'Dataset (SO).xlsx'
note: Categories that occur in Zhang et al.'s Stack Overflow sheets for the five dimensions they analysed by constant comparison (functions, purposes, benefits, limitations and challenges, expected features). Limitation and expected-feature definitions are carried over from ../../demo/ground_truth/zhang_codebook.json; purpose and benefit definitions are written from the paper's Section 4 and Tables 3-4; function definitions from the category names in Figure 2d. Categories that occur only in their GitHub data are omitted.

categories.name: Difficulty of integration
categories.definition: Copilot does not work together with the IDE or other plug-ins: after installing Copilot other plug-ins or editor features stop working, Copilot conflicts with editor shortcut settings, Copilot misbehaves or stops working inside a given editor, or Copilot cannot be integrated with an IDE because that IDE is not supported.
examples: But when I have a suggestion: And I press "Tab" to accept the suggestion, Vs Code adds a tab in the code
the copilot icon disappeared ...
Is there a way to set up GitHub copilot in Google Colab?
I am trying to run Github Copilot (copilot-mode) on ein with doom emacs, but it doesn't work for me.
Copilot only works with VSCode, VSCodium is not supported at the moment (paper, GitHub)

categories.name: Difficulty of accessing Copilot
categories.definition: The user cannot reach or activate Copilot: the Copilot server cannot be connected to, login/authentication with GitHub fails, proxies are not supported, the server is unstable, or access is restricted (e.g. by region).
examples: My IDEA plugin, 'github copilot' can't login in github. It is waiting for GitHub Authentication...
Github copilot proxy error ... Sign in failed: Proxy Authentication Required
it just showed up as ERR_CONNECTION_RESET!
I cannot connect to the GitHub account and the Copilot server in VSCode (paper, SO)

categories.name: Limitation to code generation
categories.definition: What Copilot can generate is constrained: it offers too few or too short solutions, does not generate in some languages or file types, cannot use wider context, cannot be tuned, or otherwise does not produce the generation the user needs (as opposed to generating wrong code).
examples: Copilot is limited to around 1000 characters in the response (paper, GitHub)
Copilot didn't work. Tried it in different files and languages - works everywhere but not Python
Auto closing brackets ... not working for Vue files
Can Github Copilot look at the context of a project with multiple files?

categories.name: Poor quality of generated code
categories.definition: Code or text that Copilot generates is wrong, does not work, is nonsensical or untrustworthy.
examples: Github Copilot suggest solutions that don't work (paper, SO)
GitHub Copilot getting its suggestion 95% correct, but incorrectly using format('otf')
Line-Line Intersection algorithm generated by the Github Copilot doesn't work in some instances

categories.name: Code privacy threat
categories.definition: Concern that Copilot reads, collects, uploads or leaks the user's code, secrets or personal data without permission.
examples: Copilot does collect personal data so just take precaution when working in private repos (paper, GitHub)
asked it to autocomplete the API url with the key open, and it listed suggestions with various API keys
I find it weird that he can scan everything on the computer.

categories.name: Unfriendly user experience
categories.definition: Using Copilot is annoying, distracting or interrupting: suggestions get in the way, hide other UI, or the tool has poor UX.
examples: an amazing tool with poor user experience (paper, GitHub)
The github copilot prediction code is placed above the first line of code and does not let me see it, it distracts me.
I found that to be quite interrupting
its suggestions often show first and I don't see the menu for the methods

categories.name: Lack of customization
categories.definition: The user cannot adjust Copilot's behaviour, shortcuts or settings to their needs because the option does not exist or cannot be found.
examples: My question is about setting up shortcuts in Visual Studio Code for GitHub Copilot Labs (paper, SO)
I would like to change the hotkey back but I am unable to figure out how to change the auto complete key.
I have found solutions for VSCode, but nothing for Visual Studio. When I search for copilot options I dont see any options like described.

categories.name: Difficulty of understanding the generated code
categories.definition: The user does not understand what the code Copilot generated does or why it works.
examples: I really do not understand this enough ... It was written by Copilot (paper, SO)
Confused on github copilot solution that works but not sure why
question mark operator (?) before variables - what do they do in rust? ... saw (in some Copilot suggestions)

categories.name: Hard to configure
categories.definition: Setting Copilot up or configuring it so that it works is difficult: setup never completes, configuration steps are unclear, or a changed configuration cannot be restored.
examples: Keep getting 'Your Copilot experience is not fully configured, complete your setup' in Visual Studio 2022 (paper, GitHub)
I accidentally hid Brushes and test generation sections on github copilot labs extension's window and I can't find how to fix it

categories.name: High pricing
categories.definition: Copilot costs money or is too expensive.
examples: it is too expensive (paper, GitHub)
GitHub Copilot is now payed too.

categories.name: Show loading
categories.definition: Copilot makes the editor load, hang or lock up with a loading indicator.
examples: while editing files within Visual Studio, I am periodically locking up with the following dialog showing.
When I change anything it just loads for a while and sometimes it keeps loading.

categories.name: Challenge of not providing outdated suggestions
categories.definition: Copilot may suggest outdated or deprecated APIs and library usages.
examples: making sure that the tool does not provide outdated suggestions would still be a challenge (paper, SO)

categories.name: Can be integrated with more IDEs
categories.definition: The user wants Copilot available in an IDE, editor or notebook environment it does not (yet) support.
examples: Github Copilot in SAP Business Application Studio (BAS)
How to use or integrate github copilot in monaco-editor
Will there be a version of GitHub CoPilot for "Visual Studio Code Server"?

categories.name: Give suggestions when requested
categories.definition: The user wants Copilot not to suggest automatically all the time, only when requested (e.g. via a trigger shortcut).
examples: Is it possible to not have GitHub Copilot automatically suggest code, instead only showing its suggestions when using the 'trigger inline suggestion' shortcut? (paper, SO)

categories.name: Accept the needed part of the suggestions
categories.definition: The user wants to accept only part of a suggestion (e.g. one line of several, or a word).
examples: accept one line of several (paper, SO)
I wish this existed for Visual Studio too as it's a great feature.

categories.name: Allow customization of shortcuts for suggestions
categories.definition: The user wants to change or assign the keys used to accept, trigger or navigate suggestions.
examples: Accept Github Copilot inline suggestion with right arrow key instead of tab in VSCode
Is there no way to change the copilot inline suggestion trigger hotkey in Visual Studio?
Github CoPilot should give us an option to assign a custom key instead of a [TAB] (paper, GitHub)

categories.name: Suggestions in IDE UI can be configured
categories.definition: The user wants to configure how and where suggestions are displayed in the IDE UI relative to other UI elements.
examples: In Visual Studio 2022, when GitHub Copilot suggests an inline hint, the quick suggestion widget will be suppressed ... This annoys me
The github copilot prediction code is placed above the first line of code and does not let me see it ... Is there any configuration that allows me ...

categories.name: Can be used with more development frameworks
categories.definition: The user wants Copilot to work with additional development frameworks or tools (e.g. database tools).
examples: the only options currently for copilot/ChatGPT SQL assistance is to generate queries outside of SSMS (paper-level description; sole SO instance is an overlap post)

categories.name: Ability to draw UML digrams
categories.note: [sic]: spelled as in Zhang et al., Table 6
categories.definition: The user wants Copilot to produce diagrams.
examples: Can GitHub Copilot draw diagrams?

categories.name: Ability to turn off data collection
categories.definition: The user wants to stop Copilot from collecting or seeing their code or data (e.g. opt-in per project).
examples: (sole SO instance is an overlap post; paper gives no example)

categories.name: Enable a dialog to accept or deny suggestions
categories.definition: The user wants an explicit dialog/UI to accept or reject suggestions.
examples: Enable Github Copilot "dialog" to accept or deny suggestions

categories.name: Compatible with other code generation tools
categories.definition: The user wants Copilot to work alongside other code-generation or assistance tools (e.g. ReSharper) or platforms.
examples: hoped Copilot could be compatible with other code generation tools like ReSharper (paper)
Is there a way to set up GitHub copilot in Google Colab?

categories.name: To help generate code
categories.definition: The poster uses Copilot to produce code they need, e.g. by writing steps in comments and letting Copilot fill in the code.

categories.name: To fix bugs
categories.definition: The poster turns to Copilot to find or repair a bug they could not fix themselves.

categories.name: To try out the functionality of Copilot
categories.definition: The poster installs or uses Copilot to explore what it can do, not for a specific task.

categories.name: To improve coding ability
categories.definition: The poster uses Copilot to learn language features or improve their own programming skill.

categories.name: To provide ideas for writing code
categories.definition: The poster uses Copilot's suggestions as ideas or a starting point for their own solution rather than code to accept as is.

categories.name: To generate code comments
categories.definition: The poster uses Copilot to write comments or documentation for code.

categories.name: To check the code
categories.definition: The poster uses Copilot to check whether their code is correct.

categories.name: Useful code generation
categories.definition: The poster reports that Copilot generates useful code, reducing their workload or helping when they do not know how to write something.

categories.name: Better code quality
categories.definition: The poster reports that code from Copilot is shorter, simpler or more correct than their own.

categories.name: Good adaptation to users' code patterns
categories.definition: The poster reports that Copilot adapts to their coding style or practices.

categories.name: Frequent updates to provide more features
categories.definition: The poster reports that Copilot is updated often and gains features.

categories.name: Faster development
categories.definition: The poster reports that Copilot saves time or speeds up programming.

categories.name: Better user experience
categories.definition: The poster reports that Copilot is pleasant or unobtrusive to use.

categories.name: Data processing
categories.definition: The thread describes a function implemented with Copilot's help whose job is reading, transforming or aggregating data.

categories.name: Front-end element control
categories.definition: The thread describes a function implemented with Copilot's help whose job is controlling user-interface or page elements.

categories.name: Test
categories.definition: The thread describes a function implemented with Copilot's help whose job is writing tests.

categories.name: Image processing
categories.definition: The thread describes a function implemented with Copilot's help whose job is processing or generating images.

categories.name: Algorithm
categories.definition: The thread describes a function implemented with Copilot's help whose job is implementing an algorithm.

categories.name: String processing
categories.definition: The thread describes a function implemented with Copilot's help whose job is manipulating strings.

categories.name: Text processing
categories.definition: The thread describes a function implemented with Copilot's help whose job is processing natural-language text.

categories.name: Iteration
categories.definition: The thread describes a function implemented with Copilot's help whose job is writing loops or iteration logic.

categories.name: Serialization
categories.definition: The thread describes a function implemented with Copilot's help whose job is serializing or deserializing data.

categories.name: URL building
categories.definition: The thread describes a function implemented with Copilot's help whose job is building or parsing URLs.

categories.name: Filtering
categories.definition: The thread describes a function implemented with Copilot's help whose job is filtering collections.

categories.name: Printing
categories.definition: The thread describes a function implemented with Copilot's help whose job is printing or formatting output.

categories.name: Memory read
categories.definition: The thread describes a function implemented with Copilot's help whose job is reading memory or buffers.
